title: manifest
description: One bulk-export manifest: the file the emailed link downloads since 2026-08-24, listing the export's payload as one-use download URLs - the export's index, where the pre-manifest flow delivered the payload itself. Its filename, manifest-<uuid>-<epoch>-<hex8>-<YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM-SS>.json, carries the same <uuid>-<epoch>-<hex8> core as the pre-manifest directory names (data-<uuid>-<epoch>-<hex8>-batch-NNNN), the uuid also appearing in every export_url path; the suffix changed from batch-NNNN to a datetime agreeing with created_at to the second. Prefix and suffix tell the vintages apart; the core is the export's identity in both.

instructions.description: The provider's sentence to the reader. Observed constant: download each file via its export_url, each URL usable once.

created_at.description: The manifest's creation instant, ISO-8601 with microseconds and offset; agrees to the second with the datetime suffix of the manifest's own filename. The epoch in that filename is 14-16 seconds earlier in both observed manifests; what instant it stamps, the manifests do not say.

total_files.description: The length of data_files, restated by the provider.

data_files.description: One entry per payload file, ordered by batch_index.

batch_index.description: Equals the entry's position in data_files in every observed entry of both manifests - nothing yet shows it carrying more than that. Not the pre-manifest batch-NNNN: that suffix named a whole export, this numbers entries inside one.

export_url.description: LEAKS PRIVACY (the account uuid in the path) and SPENDS: a one-use download URL - fetching it consumes it, so the URL is an ephemeral credential, not an address.

category.description: What the file holds. Closed over the categories observed 2026-08-24; a new category fails loudly by name (the ModelId precedent). conversations, memories and projects name pre-manifest components; light_metadata is new to this flow; users and login_history have no category here.

part.description: Observed 0 in every entry of both manifests, agreeing with the filename's -NNN suffix (which batch_index does not). What part counts, the manifests so far do not show.

filename.description: The payload file's name, <category>-<part padded to 3>.zip in every observed entry.

version.description: The manifest format's own version, the provider's. "1.0" observed.
